Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: No significant correlation was found between categorized serum 25(OH)D levels and depression (BDI-II) in shift nurses.
Sentence: "However, no significant correlation was observed between 25(OH)D levels and mental health when the 25(OH)D level was categorized."
Measured as: depression (BDI-II)
Population: Shift nurses (day, evening, night) in central Taiwan, mostly female
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not given)
Comparator: Categories of 25(OH)D level (deficient, inadequate)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 95
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency predicted higher odds of postnatal depression.
Sentence: "Vitamin D deficiency predicted postnatal depression (OR = 3.15), while sufficiency was associated with remission."
Measured as: postnatal depression (EPDS)
Population: Pregnant women in a public hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan, followed from 12-32 weeks gestation to 6-8 weeks postpartum
Intervention: Measured vitamin D status (deficiency), not administered
Comparator: Women without vitamin D deficiency
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 152
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are observational vitamin D studies, but one is a cross-sectional study of shift nurses with BDI-II and the other a prospective cohort of perinatal women with EPDS; the populations differ most.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["design_or_bias","outcome_measure"],"detail":"population: shift nurses in Taiwan vs pregnant/postpartum women in Pakistan; cross-sectional BDI-II vs cohort EPDS"}
